A.trend: No series is drawn; the page honestly says it cannot measure the trend, but the anchor scores no series as 0.
A.comparison: India vs China diabetes counts are from memory and labelled estimate. Only one comparator is given.
A.chart: All charts are memory or estimate-labelled.
A.dimensions: No traced chart, so the estimate charts open at most one dimension.
A.map: No map is drawn, with an honest explanation.
A.forecast: The diabetes projection is labelled estimate and its method is recomputable. The endpoint (2030 projection) is not among the plotted points.
A.drilldown: Key documents carry DOIs, but the breakdown is from memory. Follow-ups are written in words only.
A.export: The script flagged the tables as invented (ceiling 0).
A.repro: Zero numbers trace to a recorded call.
A.refs: DOIs resolve and claims are tied. No quotes are given.
A.accuracy: The recalled figures (Malik 1.26, Imamura 1.18/1.13, INDIAB 101M, NCD-RisC 212/148, Singh 184k) match the published sources and are labelled.
A.limits: Limits are specific and honest, with no corpus limits to state.
A.integrity: Four views render with zero console errors.
A.verdict: The script found an untagged number in the verdict (ceiling 0).
A.crossdomain: No corpora traced; news and patents are reported as not queried.
A.actionability: Actors are specific and the recommendation is tied to verdict and forecast. Several indicators are not defined on data in the page.

B.drilldown: Document labels plus follow-ups written in words.
B.repro: Nothing traced, and the tags are non-standard.
B.refs: Title/DOI mismatch for the INDIAB entry. Malik's figure is attributed to the Vartanian 2007 reference. The drill-down DOI is suspect.
B.accuracy: Gives INDIAB prevalence as 10.1% (published 11.4%). Misattributes the RR 1.26.
B.limits: Generic statements of what was not measured.
B.verdict: Direct, but it gives high confidence with no traced numbers.
B.actionability: Actors are named, but costs are 'not measured (est.)' and the indicators are not on the page.

C.trend: Both lanes are traced with censoring and the growth/peak are recomputed exactly. But 'not trending' for the claim-news series contradicts the tool's 'rising' (1.41).
C.comparison: India vs US/China/UK/Pakistan on lift and counts, with ratios recomputed. Lift is not read against India's 2.9% share.
C.dimensions: Seven dimensions covered, each with captions.
C.map: Two lanes are mapped with placed_pct, the patent lane is stated empty, and the Nigeria lift is flagged. The England journal-country row is not caught.
C.forecast: Traced central and bounds, baseline, MAE 39 vs 41.6, gap to today, sensitivity-not-CI, and a tie to the decision.
C.drilldown: Themes, countries and documents with DOIs; seven follow-ups executed ok. Some theme items are mis-stated.
C.repro: All 157 numbers traced. A few drill-down values do not match c13.
C.refs: Eight resolving DOIs with verbatim quotes. The r3 author names are not in the record.
C.accuracy: Says 'nigeria (76)' where the c13 tag shows 25. A 27-article taxation subcategory is not in c13. 'Critical' is relabelled as 'high-priority'.
C.integrity: Ten of ten views render with zero errors.
C.crossdomain: Two quantified connections, patents stated empty, and the forecast is used in the recommendation.
C.actionability: Strong rows and gap queries. The indicators (news counts, paper counts) are weak proxies for policy outcomes.

D.trend: Both lanes with censoring. The text says May 2026 had 2 articles but the chart shows 22. No research growth factor is given.
D.comparison: India 0.13× the US and 1.88× China with shares and placed_pct. No lift.
D.chart: Charts traced, but the news reading contradicts the plotted May 2026 value, and the bar chart duplicates the map quantity.
D.dimensions: Time, geography, composition and forecast are traced. The comparison bars duplicate the map.
D.map: One lane mapped with placed_pct; the first-author and patent lanes are stated in text. Lift is not read.
D.forecast: Traced, with baseline, MAE 4.95 vs 5.06, gap to today and quantity defined. The decision tie is thin.
D.drilldown: Follow-ups are in words and not executable.
D.repro: Traced, but there is an internal text–chart mismatch.
D.refs: DOIs resolve and quotes are verbatim fragments. Tags mix c and r ids.
D.accuracy: Text–chart contradiction on May 2026, and the 45-vs-56 thirds figure is implausible.
D.integrity: Renders cleanly, but depends on a local map file.
D.verdict: All four fields are present. The contrary item is a retrieval artefact rather than evidence.
D.crossdomain: Four corpora with connecting sentences, but the mismatch is not quantified.
D.actionability: Indicators are not defined on series in the page, and comparators do not inform the option choice.

A: The manifest chart's ref:r1 source covers Imamura points, which are r2
B: RR 1.26 (Malik 2010) attributed to the Vartanian 2007 reference
2011 INDIAB title paired with the 2023 DOI
Diabetes Care DOI 10.2337/dc09-1519 is likely wrong
C: 'nigeria (76)' in the drill-down where c13 shows 25
'government taxation and revenue systems (27 articles)' is not in c13
The critical tally (384) is relabelled as the 'high-priority band'
Claim-news series called 'not trending' where the tool's direction is 'rising'
D: Text says May 2026 had 2 articles; the plotted point is 22
The early-vs-late thirds of 45 vs 56 are inconsistent with monthly values around 20–30

raw.verdict: C alone grounds the decision in traced research, news and geography data across both lanes, with a backtested forecast and India-vs-comparator lift, though some drill-down figures are mis-stated. D is traced but thinner and contains an internal text–chart contradiction. A is an honest, accurate memory brief with labelled estimates, and B adds little beyond the health claim, with citation and prevalence errors.
